learning_outcomes.text: To provide students with theoretical knowledge and practical familiarity with the basic methods of synthesis and macromolecular characterization of polymers and colloids.
Theoretical and practical training of students in basic techniques for studying the thermal and surface properties of soft materials.
Preparation of students for the completion of a thesis or postgraduate studies.
Development of interdisciplinary and critical thinking
Searching for, analyzing, and synthesizing data and information, using the necessary technologies
Practical familiarization with methods and techniques
Promotion of free, creative, and inductive thinking

syllabus_topics: Introduction: Types of Polymers, Colloids, Nomenclature, Polymerization Techniques, Molecular Weight, Size-Shape of Polymers, Applications
Polymerization Methods & Polymer Reactions: Stepwise, Free Radical, Ion, Copolymerization
Molecular Characterization of Polymers: Determination of Absolute Molecular Weight (Static Light Scattering)
Size Exclusion Chromatography (SEC)
Viscometry
Thermal Properties: Crystallization, Glass Transition, Elastomers, Transition Determination Methods
Surface Properties: Interfacial Tension, Young's Equation, Contact Angle, Wettability
Synthesis of Soft Materials
Preparation of Homopolymer Polystyrene Using the Free Radical Mass Polymerization Technique

Preparation of Random Copolymer Polystyrene-co-poly (butyl methacrylate) using the Free Radical Solution Polymerization Technique and Nylon 6.10 using the Two-Phase Polycondensation Polymerization Technique
Synthesis of Polystyrene Colloidal Particles Using the Emulsion Polymerization Technique
Preparation of Random Polymeric Acrylic Acid Network
Characterization of Soft Materials
Study of Molecular Weight Distribution by Size Exclusion Chromatography (SEC)
Structural and Morphological Characterization of Polymers Using Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC)
Thermal Resistance of Polymers and Composite Materials Using Thermogravimetric Analysis (TGA)
Modification of the Wettability of a Solid Surface by Depositing Polymeric Materials and Measuring the Contact Angle
Biomaterials
Drug delivery with the aid of polymers: release of salicylic acid from poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid)
Isolation of Milk Proteins and Quantitative Determination of Proteins by Bradford
teaching_methods: Communication via the Department's website and email
Guidance on using reliable scientific online sources to find bibliography and present topics

assessment_methods.method: Final written exam (problem solving and essay questions)

assessment_rules: Students are assessed through written tests, questions during laboratory exercises, graded laboratory reports, and a final written exam combining problem solving and essay questions. An oral exam is possible for students with learning difficulties. Students can review their written exam after results are released and ask questions. The specific assessment method and percentage weights are described in the first lecture and posted on the course website.
